reference: Contract expectations come from Bash's documented type/help builtins and the exact blockdev builtin synopsis and help strings in the published source contract The source docs describe a syscall shim, and the published source contract is present, but this harness does not load that module; the documented sol-blockdev-check.py driver is absent from the documented source tree. No blockdev operation is run here: both the candidate and util-linux command issue kernel ioctls. Deferred operations specify an isolated syscall-mock requirement.
coverage: The candidate registers blockdev as a Bash builtin.
Bash help exposes the blockdev synopsis and all ten documented action names.
Metadata only; operation coverage is zero. Deferred cases are future qualification requirements.
exclusions: No blockdev action is executed, including query-only actions, because it reaches the kernel open/ioctl path and no reviewed mock is supplied to this runner.
Real block-device geometry, driver behavior, privilege checks, flush effects, and partition-table reread effects require separate disposable-VM or syscall-mock qualification.

cases.purpose: Check through Bash type metadata that the candidate registered blockdev as a builtin, without invoking it.
Check that Bash help has a synopsis containing the documented command name and device operand.
Check that Bash help documents each of the ten blockdev action options listed by the implementation contract.
cases.script:
doc=$(help blockdev)
for action in --getsz --getsize64 --getsize --getss --getbsz --getro --setro --setrw --flushbufs --rereadpt; do
  case "$doc" in
    *"$action"*) ;;
    *) exit 1 ;;
  esac
done
printf 'all-ten-actions-documented\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise query ioctl dispatch and formatting for size in sectors, size in bytes, legacy size, logical sector size, block size, and normalized read-only state.
cases.reason: Query ioctls need a block device: uid 2000 with setgroups([]) cannot open /dev/loop-control or /dev/loopN (root:disk 0660), cannot mknod block nodes (CAP_MKNOD; device nodes are refused inside user namespaces), and the real virtio disk nodes are root:disk 0660, so no block device with known contents is visible to an unprivileged fixture. Read-only query ioctls themselves need no capability once a readable node exists, so only device provisioning is missing; r5 values cannot exist on a real device.

cases.purpose: Exercise ordered --getro, --setro, --getro, --setrw, --getro sequences across fixture devices and invocations.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: printed values 0/1/0 and setter values need a buffer-writing mock or a block device; r2: unchanged: per-device persistent state needs a block device or stateful mock; r3: unchanged: kernel EACCES for BLKROSET needs a block device

cases.purpose: Exercise --flushbufs and --rereadpt dispatch, zero-argument ioctl requests, device iteration, and continuation order.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: real permitted/denied BLKFLSBUF needs a block device (BLOCK-DEV); r2: unchanged: partition re-read effect needs a loop device with partscan (BLOCK-DEV)

cases.purpose: Exercise missing/open-failing paths, EACCES read-write retry, ioctl failure continuation, descriptor close handling, and aggregate status.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r4: close(2) failure injection not attempted: no stable descriptor-number condition for a seccomp rule; r5: Descriptor counts are unchanged for the tested open/ioctl failures. Close-error cleanup and real successful device paths remain untested.
